title: Eventual flatness of finitely presented algebraic spaces
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is finitely presented if it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact), and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, let $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transition maps, and let $T=\varprojlim_i T_i$. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a finitely presented morphism $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ of an algebraic space to $T_{i_0}$. For $i\ge i_0$ put $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, $f_i:X_i\to T_i$, and put $X=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$, $f:X\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Flatness of morphisms of algebraic spaces is tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. If $f$ is flat, there is $i\ge i_0$ such that $f_j$ is flat for every $j\ge i$.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), last assertion, in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), specialized to a finitely presented space over an affine base; persistence at later stages: spaces-morphisms.tex, Tag 03MO (lemma-base-change-flat).

proof.text: The affine scheme $T_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Use the quasi-compactness conventions now explicit in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]: pull back the quasi-compact morphism $f_{i_0}$ along the identity of the quasi-compact algebraic space $T_{i_0}$. Its source $X_{i_0}$ is therefore quasi-compact and admits a surjective etale map $c:C\to X_{i_0}$ from a quasi-compact scheme $C$. Apply [lem-a1-qc-map-affine-etale-neighbourhood] to this $c$, over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. It supplies an affine scheme $U_{i_0}$ and an etale map $u:U_{i_0}\to X_{i_0}$ such that $C\times_{X_{i_0}}U_{i_0}\to C$ is surjective. Use the field-valued point convention stated in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] to check surjectivity of $u$: a field-valued point of $X_{i_0}$ lifts to $C$ after a field extension, then to the displayed fibre product after a further field extension, and projection gives a lift to $U_{i_0}$. This proves that $u$ is an affine-source surjective etale atlas, including when $X_{i_0}$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), choosing a surjective etale affine source atlas. Quasi-compactness convention: spaces-properties.tex Tag 03E3 (definition-quasi-compact); the affine choice is the conclusion of Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover), obtained here from the existing stronger affine-neighbourhood node.

proof.text: Set $U_j=U_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_j$ and $U=U_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$. For $B=T_j$ or $T$, write $X_B=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}B$. On any test scheme the maps $(a,b)\mapsto(a,(u\circ a,b))$ and $(a,(x,b))\mapsto(a,b)$ are inverse: the latter input satisfies $x=u\circ a$. They are natural in the test scheme and identify $U_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}B$ with $U_{i_0}\times_{X_{i_0}}X_B$, compatibly with both projections. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], arbitrary algebraic-space base change preserves the surjective etale atlas $u$, giving surjective etale maps $U_j\to X_j$ and $U\to X$. The affine-limit formula in [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] makes $T$ affine; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] makes every $U_j$ and $U$ an affine scheme.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), base-changed diagrams; affine target specialization. See limits.tex Tags 01YX/01YW and schemes.tex affine-spectrum fibre products.

proof.text: Write $g_{i_0}:U_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ for the composite with $f_{i_0}$, and let $g_j:U_j\to T_j$ and $g:U\to T$ be its base changes. Apply the chart-testing assertion of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] with the surjective etale source atlas $u$ of step 1 and the identity chart of the scheme target $T_{i_0}$. Finite presentation of $f_{i_0}$ includes local finite presentation, so this gives local finite presentation of $g_{i_0}$. Apply the same assertion to $f:X\to T$ using the surjective etale source atlas $U\to X$ of step 2 and the identity chart of $T$: flatness of $f$ gives flatness of $g$. The added quasi-compactness and point-set conventions in the current cited statement impose no properness, initial-stage flatness, or transition-map flatness hypothesis in either application.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), final paragraph: chartwise flatness and local finite presentation; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03ML (definition-flat), 03MM (lemma-flat-local), 03XP (definition-locally-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] with base system $(T_j)$, initial index $i_0$, source $U_{i_0}$, target $T_{i_0}$, and morphism $g_{i_0}$ over $T_{i_0}$. The base, source, and target at this index are all affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The transition morphisms are affine by hypothesis, local finite presentation and flatness after base change were established in step 3, and the required limiting cone is the given $T$. Projection identifies $T_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$ with $T$, so the theorem gives $i\ge i_0$ with $g_i:U_i\to T_i$ flat.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), reduction to the scheme result, here using limits.tex Tag 04AI (lemma-descend-flat-finite-presentation) for its morphism-only conclusion.

proof.text: The surjective etale atlas $U_i\to X_i$ of step 2 and flatness of $g_i$ imply flatness of $f_i$, by chart testing in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Now fix $j\ge i$. The morphism $f_j$ is the base change of $f_i$ along $T_j\to T_i$: on a test scheme both source descriptions amount to maps to $X_{i_0}$ and $T_j$ agreeing over $T_{i_0}$, so $X_i\times_{T_i}T_j\cong X_j$ compatibly with the maps to $T_j$. Arbitrary base-change stability of flatness in that same cited node proves $f_j$ flat. Thus the single index $i$ works for every $j\ge i$. If $X_{i_0}$ is empty, all source spaces are empty and the chart tests are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 08K0 (lemma-descend-flat), return from charts to spaces; persistence from spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MO (lemma-base-change-flat), and chart testing Tag 03MM (lemma-flat-local).

split_report.summary: Proved eventual flatness in five steps along Stacks 08K0: construct an affine-source surjective etale atlas; base change the atlas; test local finite presentation and flatness on it; apply scheme descent 04AI; return to spaces and preserve flatness at all later stages. No item statement change, new node, Mathlib leaf, or Lean edit. Repair of returned head 7a8aaa75c91: compared every statement and proof dependency with current main 3553e176845; only lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality changed. Its old chart-testing and arbitrary-base-change clauses are unchanged, but it now makes point-set, quasi-compactness and representable closed-immersion conventions explicit. Reworked step 1 to use its new quasi-compactness convention directly (and the existing affine-qcqs lemma), replacing the older affine-test convention from lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local.
